citations.narrative:
During the inspection, two (2) young serval kittens who were not authorized for exhibit on the current license, were
present on the premises. The facility representative stated they were placed on exhibit on/around September 5th, 2026.
The animals were housed next to the other regulated animals and the facility's current license does not authorize the
exhibition of wild/exotic felids. Failure to acquire authorization for specific groups of animals does not ensure that the
facility is knowledgeable and capable of maintaining compliance with the care, husbandry, housing, and handling of these
species.
Licenses must specifically authorize the use of wild/exotic felids, and a licensee must obtain a new license before using
any animal beyond those types or numbers of animals authorized under the existing license. The licensee must obtain a
new license authorizing the use of wild/exotic felids for regulated purposes.
Correct by removing the servals from exhibit until a new license is obtained authorizing the use of wild/exotic felids.
Correct from this date forward, Sept. 23, 2026.
This inspection and exit interview were conducted with facility representative.
You may appeal all or part of any inspection report by submitting a written statement contesting the findings—along with
any supporting documentation—to the Deputy Administrator. Appeals of routine, focused, or attempted inspections must
be received within 21 days of report issuance as shown by the signature line of this report.
Appeals may be sent by email to AnimalCare@usda.gov.
Appeals sent by mail should be addressed to:
Deputy Administrator
APHIS Animal Care (AC)
U.S. Department of Agriculture
2150 Centre Avenue, Building B
Mailstop #3W11
Fort Collins, CO 80526-8117
Additional Inspectors:
